title: The Long Road Ahead
subtitle: The hammer of history strikes the anvil, yet the marks it makes will soon be smoothed away.

trails.title: Administrative Complaint
trails.description: Some Foundation staff have been complaining about rats on this floor lately. Pure nonsense.

content.text: I'm sorry, but I think it's time you left.
There will be little more to see here.
But the war isn't over yet.

branch.text: Earthquakes, floods, famine, plague, robbery, car crashes, a slip in the shower ...
War is just one catastrophe among many.
At least, this war is not.
Next time? Are you so intrigued by the life of a pension-drawn widow?
I would decline, but my upbringing demands otherwise. How unfortunate ...
Well ... perhaps it's better to drink dirty water beneath the eaves than to eat dust on the battlefield.
That is all. Hurry along to the eastern front. Check on your friend. I will pray for her.

items.text: The Long Road Ahead

items.speaker: Marsha
items.text: My mission on the Eastern Front is over, but the battle that took place here has left an indelible impression on me. It still strikes me like lightning.

items.speaker: Marsha
items.text: In the city of Bereggrad, civilians, barely knowing how to handle a gun, gave their all to defend their homes from bandits and Manus Vindictae.

items.speaker: Marsha
items.text: Their unyielding defense of the city streets bought crucial tactical space for the Zeno Cavalry Corps and their allies on the field, allowing them to strike the enemy's main force without restraint.

items.speaker: Marsha
items.text: Some lost their lives, but many more will live because of their sacrifice. I am certain those names will be remembered on this steppe forever.

items.speaker: Marsha
items.text: As an aside, I ran into Charon here—what are the odds of that? It's a shame I don't have time to share more stories with you in just one letter.

items.speaker: Marsha
items.text: I hope one day to tell you all about them in person. And don't worry about me, my dear Marianne: I'll soon return to the Foundation headquarters. I look forward to hearing from you.

items.speaker: Yermolai
items.text: That the only letter you want to send?
The knight folds her letter, seals it in an envelope, and presses the Foundation's wax seal on it with solemn care.

items.speaker: Marsha
items.text: I would've written more if I knew you'd be delivering them personally.

items.speaker: Marsha
items.text: If you're returning to the Western Front, please bring this letter to Montpaix. Someone there will pick it up.

items.speaker: Yermolai
items.text: Ah, you mean that Gargoyle girl, right? She's not hanging around Montpaix anymore.

items.speaker: Marsha
items.text: Huh? Do you know where she went?

items.speaker: Yermolai
items.text: Can't say that I do, but I have run into her a few times since.
Hound looks as though a chill has just run up his spine.

items.speaker: Yermolai
items.text: First time was in Luxembourg. I was out looking for something when she decided to press the muzzle of her gun against the back of my head.

items.speaker: Yermolai
items.text: I thought she was still holding a grudge over what happened at Hill 299. I wouldn't blame her. After all, Creius owes her a hell of a lot more than a little thanks.

items.speaker: Yermolai
items.text: But turns out she just wanted to have a chat with a member of the "XII."

items.speaker: Marsha
items.text: What did you talk about?

items.speaker: Yermolai
items.text: Something about setting rules. Said she doesn't mind helping out when her objectives overlap with ours.

items.speaker: Yermolai
items.text: On the condition that we share with her each and every piece of information we have. Must've been serious, right? Doesn't seem like the kind of person who appreciates a joke.

items.speaker: Marsha
items.text: Maybe just your jokes.

items.speaker: Yermolai
items.text: Ha, could be. Anyway, I don't know her exact whereabouts, but finding her again shouldn't be too hard. I'm sure she wouldn't wanna miss your letter.

items.speaker: Marsha
items.text: Thanks. So, why were you sent here?

items.speaker: Yermolai
items.text: Creius wanted me to do some "mopping up." Lucky me, always stuck with the chores.

items.speaker: Yermolai
items.text: Watching to see if the Zeno corps here shows any "unusual political tendencies" after the battle. Making sure they've cut contact with Igor. Oh, and Blackbird!
He pulls a document from his coat and hands it to Marsha. After a pause, she carefully opens it.

items.speaker: Marsha
items.text: "Merel, head to the Don River region immediately. Cover your tracks and investigate the Golden Famine there. Creius. November ... 10th"?

items.speaker: Marsha
items.text: That was before Merel's desertion. Then, she didn't run away after all?

items.speaker: Yermolai
items.text: Nah, the date's fake. Creius wrote up this "secret order" right in front of me after your report.

items.speaker: Yermolai
items.text: The seal on the signature hadn't even dried when I set out.
A little paperwork filed after the fact. Should be harmless.

items.speaker: Marsha
items.text: I see. Are you sure you should've told me this?
Yermolai's face darkens unexpectedly.

items.speaker: Yermolai
items.text: We're on the same team.

items.speaker: Yermolai
items.text: If we can't trust each other, we'll all end up in the ditch when s**t hits the fan. Know what I mean?

items.speaker: Marsha
items.text: You make a good point. Merel's still resting. Should I call for her now?

items.speaker: Merel
items.text: I-I'm here.
The deserter, spared for now by this "secret order," peeks out from behind Marsha with a sheepish look on her face.
Yermolai tilts his chin at her.

items.speaker: Yermolai
items.text: Your days of fluttering under a babysitter's wings have come to an end, Blackbird. You may be off the Foundation's hook, but I'm afraid some form of internal punishment within the squad is inevitable.

items.speaker: Merel
items.text: Internal punishment?
Hearing this, Merel takes a slow step back.

items.speaker: Yermolai
items.text: Don't think you can get away again.
Like catching a rabbit, the man pulls Merel out from behind the knight.

items.speaker: Merel
items.text: Naah!

items.speaker: Marsha
items.text: Hey, go easy on her!

items.speaker: Yermolai
items.text: I'll be keeping tabs on her from now on, Marsha. Even got a tracking serum. Creius's order.

items.speaker: Marsha
items.text: Tracking serum?

items.speaker: Yermolai
items.text: Yeah, goof-juice invented by some eggheads. Still in development, actually. Our little runaway will make the perfect lab rat.

items.speaker: Merel
items.text: I won't run again. Trust me. I swear!

items.speaker: Yermolai
items.text: Keep that voice down. You trying to tell the entire world you're a deserter? Or you looking for a taste of Dumbitter Potion?

items.speaker: Merel
items.text: N-No.
She bites her lip.
Marsha gives her a light pat on the shoulder.

items.speaker: Marsha
items.text: Relax. I'll be traveling back with you.

items.speaker: Andreas
items.text: *neigh*

items.speaker: Merel
items.text: Huh?
A black warhorse trots over from down the street, his old friend beside him.

items.speaker: Charon
items.text: It is good that you've returned to your friends, Merel. May your journey ahead be a safe one.

items.speaker: Charon
items.text: And thank you, Marsha. Tending to this broken body must have taken a great toll on you. I am sorry for any pain it caused.

items.speaker: Marsha
items.text: Please, don't think of it that way, Charon. I can handle my arcane skills. I'm just relieved that you're back on your feet.

items.speaker: Yermolai
items.text: Gotta say, I was surprised to hear you'd made it out this way, gravedigger. Paravyan told me it was you who covered Merel's tracks.

items.speaker: Merel
items.text: W-Wait! Leave Charon out of this! I asked, I mean, I forced him to help me!

items.speaker: Yermolai
items.text: What's got you so worked up? All you did was follow Creius's orders and cover your tracks, right?

items.speaker: Merel
items.text: Umm, yeah, no, wait, did I?

items.speaker: Yermolai
items.text: Yeah, you did, and keep that in mind if anyone asks.

items.speaker: Merel
items.text: O-Okay.
Charon, struggling to follow the conversation among the "XII" Squad, gives up trying.

items.speaker: Charon
items.text: Life must flee death. It is our most basic instinct. Death is impartial, unstoppable. No creature should be punished for running from its shadow.

items.speaker: Yermolai
items.text: Sure, sure. Don't worry. I'll make sure our friend here stays safe and sound.

items.speaker: Charon
items.text: A small hope in this gray world. Now, there is more work to be done.

items.speaker: Marsha
items.text: You're leaving again, Charon?

items.speaker: Merel
items.text: Why don't you join us at the—
"Foundation" catches in her throat.

items.speaker: Merel
items.text: N-Never mind.

items.speaker: Merel
items.text: I hope I see you again, Charon, though maybe not on another battlefield. I'd be happy to never see another corpse in my life.

items.speaker: Merel
items.text: I'll miss you too, Andreas.
Merel stands on tiptoes, wrapping her arms around Andreas's neck, and presses her cheek to his rough mane.

items.speaker: Merel
items.text: Goodbye, friends! I've made so many happy memories with you, well, aside from the drowning.

items.speaker: Merel
items.text: I'll miss you from the bottom of my heart!

items.speaker: Andreas
items.text: Neigh ...

items.speaker: Charon
items.text: May our reunion come in a more peaceful time.
Leading Andreas by the reins, Charon makes his way out of the city.
They disappear into the winter grassland, returning to the long, hard road they must walk.
